# Adjudication Task — Chapter 4

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃4화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|장삼은 산적이다.
  6|
  7|생전 오대산(五臺山) 인근을 벗어난 적 없는 토박이였고 약관 무렵부터 만만한 산객들을 대상으로 통행료를 뜯어내 왔다.
  8|
  9|밤낮을 가리지 않는 성실 영업 덕분인지 언제부턴가 천력부 장삼, 하면 제법 알아주었다.
 10|
 11|오늘도 그랬다. 꼭두새벽부터 일어나 충실한 다섯 부하, 오색귀(五色鬼)를 거느리고 영업을 나왔는데…… 이상하게 발걸음이 멈추지 않는다.
 12|
 13|앞마당인 오대산을 한참 벗어나 얼마나 걸었을까, 마침내 발걸음이 멈췄을 때 저 멀리 다가오는 마차가 보였다.
 14|
 15|‘어쩌다 여기까지 왔지?’
 16|
 17|귀신에 홀렸나? 장삼은 어리둥절했지만 고급스러운 사두마차를 본 순간 자신의 직업 정신이 깨어나는 것을 느꼈다.
 18|
 19|‘저건 꼭 뺏어야 해.’
 20|
 21|장삼과 오색귀가 길을 막아서자 마부가 고삐를 잡아당겼다.
 22|
 23|털에 윤기가 자르르 흐르는 준마 네 마리가 콧김을 뿜어내며 멈췄다. 척 봐도 마리당 천 냥은 거뜬하게 나올 물건들이다.
 24|
 25|오늘은 일진이 좋군. 장삼은 흐뭇하게 웃으며 도끼를 고쳐 잡았다. 자, 이제 단전에 힘을 빡 주고. 하나, 둘.
 26|
 27|“돈 내놔!”
 28|
 29|
 30|
 31|* * *
 32|
 33|
 34|
 35|발성 뭐야, 성악가야?
 36|
 37|하지만 이 정도로는 눈 하나 깜짝 안 한다. 헌터 외길 인생 7년에 산전수전 공중전까지 다 겪은 나다.
 38|
 39|……근데 좀 무섭다.
 40|
 41|“총 여섯 명. 매복은 없어 보입니다.”
 42|
 43|마부는 비밀 요원처럼 침착한 목소리로 상황을 전달했다.
 44|
 45|이 아저씨는 믿는 구석이라도 있나. 왜 이렇게 여유롭지.
 46|
 47|물끄러미 바라보자 머리를 긁적인다.
 48|
 49|“간혹 있는 일입니다. 이 근방에서는 처음이지만요.”
 50|
 51|“왜요?”
 52|
 53|“왜긴요. 어지간한 대형 산채가 아닌 이상 무림세가를 건드리는 건 자살행위나 다름없습니다. 태원진가의 앞마당에서 도적질이라니, 어느 간 큰 놈들인지 궁금하군요.”
 54|
 55|‘누구긴. 튜토리얼 NPC지.’
 56|
 57|그보다 태원진가의 앞마당 운운하는 걸 보니 제법 가까운 거리인가 보다.
 58|
 59|‘시간을 끌어 볼까?’
 60|
 61|현재 내 경지는 이류.
 62|
 63|스탯 분배 후 느껴지는 체감은 F급 헌터의 그것을 뛰어넘지만, 무림에서 먹힐 만한 수준인지는 모르겠다.
 64|
 65|6 대 1. 마부까지 끼워 넣어도 6 대 2.
 66|
 67|‘될까?’
 68|
 69|중과부적이라는 말이 괜히 있는 게 아니다. 손발이 묶이는 순간 골로 간다.
 70|
 71|“목적지까지 얼마나 남았습니까?”
 72|
 73|“거의 다 왔습니다. 앞으로 반 시진이면 충분합니다.
 74|
 75|반 시진이면…… 한 시간이나 남았다고?
 76|
 77|짐작은 했지만 마부와 나의 ‘가깝다’는 서로 기준이 달랐다.
 78|
 79|‘거의 다 오기는 무슨.’
 80|
 81|대륙 배경이라 그런가. 스케일이 다르다, 스케일이.
 82|
 83|어쨌든 그렇다면 이제 증원군은 없는 셈 쳐야 한다. 그나마 다행인 것은 혼자가 아니라는 점이다.
 84|
 85|시종일관 여유로운 태도를 보이는 마부는 고수의 냄새를 풍겼다. 지금처럼.
 86|
 87|“제가 처리할까요?”
 88|
 89|그러면서 말채찍을 말아 쥐는데, 채찍질 한 번으로 산적들의 뼈와 살을 분리시킬 기세다.
 90|
 91|‘고수다!’
 92|
 93|그럼 그렇지. 내가 명색이 명문세가의 후계자요, 홍화루의 특급 고객인데 평범한 마부를 보내 줬을 리가 있나.
 94|
 95|‘월화가 신경 써 줬구나. 얼굴만 예쁜 게 아니라 마음도 예쁘네.’
 96|
 97|불안감이 사라지고 절로 흐뭇한 웃음이 지어진다. 내 웃음을 승낙의 의미로 받아들인 마부가 돌아섰을 때, 두 번째 고함이 터져 나왔다.
 98|
 99|“이놈들! 이 천력부의 말이 들리지 않느냐!”
100|
101|마차 창문 너머로 넘겨다보니 거대한 양날 도끼를 든 털북숭이가 소리를 치고 있었다. 우람한 상반신에 팔다리가 기둥처럼 두껍다.
102|
103|하지만 마부는 가소롭다는 듯이 중얼거렸다.
104|
105|“하룻강아지 같은 놈들이 어딜 감히.”
106|
107|캬, 기세에 취한다.
108|
109|그리고 마부의 준엄한 질타가 시작됐다.
110|
111|“양민의 고혈을 빨아먹는 산적 따위가 감히 뉘 앞을 막아서느냐! 네놈을 관아로 압송하여 지엄한 국법으로 다스려 주마!”
112|
113|판관 포청천 뺨치는 연설이었지만 털북숭이, 천력부와 그 부하들은 그리 감동한 것 같지 않았다.
114|
115|“그래, 막아섰다. 이제 어쩔래?”
116|
117|“무수한 악행을 저질러 온 네놈들의 눈알을 파내고 사지를 절구로 빻아 그 가루를 구주에 뿌려 주마! 또한 구족을 멸하여…….”
118|
119|……형벌 수위가 장난이 아닌데. 거의 역모죄다, 역모죄.
120|
121|내 생각을 읽은 것처럼 천력부가 입을 열었다.
122|
123|“거, 안에 황족 나리라도 타셨소? 듣고 있자니 오금이 저려서 못 참겠네. 그 귀하신 얼굴 구경 좀 합시다.”
124|
125|“이분의 정체를 알면 지금 물러나지 않은 것을 후회하게 될 것이다!”
126|
127|“알겠어. 알겠으니까 이제 좀 나와 보라고.”
128|
129|“어리석은 놈들……!”
130|
131|마부가 혀를 차며 내게 고개를 돌렸다. 이제 드디어 진짜 무림 고수의 활약을 볼 수 있는 건가 싶어 가슴이 두근거린다.
132|
133|“공자님. 나와 보셔야 할 것 같습니다.”
134|
135|“응?”
136|
137|나? 나 왜?
138|
139|“관을 봐야 눈물을 흘릴 놈들입니다. 감히 공자의 앞을 막아서다니, 고수를 몰라본 죗값을 똑똑히 치르겠군요.”
140|
141|그러면서 결의에 찬 표정으로 마차 문을 열어 준다.
142|
143|“진천검(振天劍)의 위명은 익히 들었습니다. 불과 약관의 나이로 절정의 경지에 오른 천재 검수! 공자의 이야기를 들을 때마다 늙은 제 가슴이 얼마나 떨렸는지 모릅니다.”
144|
145|……진천검? 천재 검수?
146|
147|‘뭐라는 거야.’
148|
149|머리가 뒤죽박죽이다. 진천검은 누구고, 절정에 오른 천재 검수는 누구며 이 마부는 뭐 하는 새끼인가?
150|
151|처리하겠다며. 당신 고수 아니었어?
152|
153|“이놈들! 이분이 누구신지 알아보겠느냐!”
154|
155|틀렸다. 마부는 핸들이 고장 난 8톤 트럭처럼 폭주 중이다.
156|
157|안 돼, 그만해. 멈춰!
158|
159|마부의 손목을 꽉 움켜잡자 그가 나를 돌아본다.
160|
161|다 안다는 듯한 웃음. 무한한 신뢰의 눈빛.
162|
163|“자, 잠깐만. 저는 진…….”
164|
165|내가 뭐라 할 틈도 없이 쩌렁쩌렁한 외침이 터져 나왔다.
166|
167|“태원진가의 이공자, 산서성을 떨어 울리는 절정 고수! 진천검 진무경 공자이시다!”
168|
169|“저는 진……태경인데요.”
170|
171|순간, 싸늘한 찬바람이 불었다.
172|
173|“예?”
174|
175|“그러니까 저는 진무경이 아니라 진태경이고 이공자가 아니라 삼공자…….”
176|
177|“……삼공자? 바로 그 삼공자?”
178|
179|그래, 이 양반아.
180|
181|마부의 동공이 흔들린다. 진도 8.0의 강진이다.
182|
183|“그, 그럼 진무경 공자는요.”
184|
185|“저야 모르죠.”
186|
187|이 시간이면 자고 있지 않을까?
188|
189|마부는 나라 잃은 표정으로 나를 바라보다가 바람 빠진 풍선 인형처럼 쓰러졌다. 졸도다.
190|
191|‘시바. 고수는 무슨.’
192|
193|마부의 손목을 놔줬다.
194|
195|닭 뼈처럼 가느다란 손목이다. 잡는 순간부터 뭔가 쎄하다 싶었다. 그렇게 허세를 부려 놓고 일반인이라니.
196|
197|“으하, 으하하하!”
198|
199|산적들이 자지러지게 웃었다. 나? 언제 식은땀이 났는지 벌써 등허리가 축축하다.
200|
201|‘이거, 진짜 재수 없으면.’
202|
203|죽음이란 단어는 차마 꺼내지 못하고 꿀꺽 삼켰다.
204|
205|나는 긴장 어린 눈으로 산적들을 훑었다.
206|
207|시발. 차라리 고블린 여섯 마리랑 싸우고 말지. 저런 덩치들을 내가 어떻게 이겨…… 어라?
208|
209|“엥?”
210|
211|뭐야, 기분 탓인가? 하지만 아무리 봐도 기분 탓이 아니다.
212|
213|우람한 상반신, 두꺼운 팔다리. 그리고…… 짧다.
214|
215|옆에 다섯 놈도 별반 다르지 않다. 천력부는 몸이라도 좋지, 이놈들은 아무리 봐도 ‘건장한’이라는 단어와는 오백 광년쯤 차이가 있다.
216|
217|그러니까 산적들의 체격이 꼭…….
218|
219|“고블린이네?”
220|
221|고블린이여?
222|
223|예상치 못한 상황에 잠시 멍해 있다가 갑자기 날아오는 도끼에 정신을 차렸다. 머릿수도 많은 새끼들이 선제공격까지 하다니.
224|
225|“야, 야! 잠깐만 타임!”
226|
227|그 순간 도끼가 그대로 10m 앞 땅에 처박혔다. 아니, 고꾸라졌다. 도끼를 날린 산적이 쑥스러운 듯이 뒤통수를 긁적였다.
228|
229|“조금 더 위로 던졌어야 했나?”
230|
231|……이거 어쩌면.
232|
233|‘살 수 있겠는데?’
234|
235|7년 동안 가장 많이 상대한 몬스터를 꼽자면 고블린이다.
236|
237|그러다 보니 놈들에 관한 모든 것을 속속들이 알게 됐다. 견습 헌터 시절에 주력 무기로 창을 선택한 것도 그 이유였다. 공격 범위에서 엄청난 우위를 점할 수 있으니까.
238|
239|마침 산적들이 딱 그 정도 체격이다. 내 눈에는 산적이 아니라 고블린 여섯 마리로 보인다. 천력부는 대장 고블린 정도?
240|
241|‘나머지 다섯은 고블린보다 약할 수도 있고.’
242|
243|고블린은 독침이라도 잘 쏘지. 방금 도끼 던지는 꼴을 보아하니 촉이 온다. 촉이 와.
244|
245|나는 바짝 마른 입술을 핥은 다음 두 손을 번쩍 들어 올렸다.
246|
247|항복 의사에 몇 놈은 당황하고 천력부는 전역한 아들을 보는 아버지처럼 흐뭇하게 웃었다.
248|
249|“기특한 놈일세.”
250|
251|‘그래, 많이 웃어 둬라.’
252|
253|한 발, 두 발. 천천히 30m에 이르는 거리를 좁혀 나간다.
254|
255|일정한 보폭과 균형 잡힌 자세로. 한 발에 한 호흡. 입에서 김이 새벽 공기를 뚫고 새어 나왔다.
256|
257|단순히 발을 내딛는 것만으로도 느껴진다.
258|
259|‘다르다!’
260|
261|다시 한번 깨달았다.
262|
263|이 게임에서의 나는, 현실의 나보다 강하다.
264|
265|가슴이 뛴다. 동시에 경각심이 고개를 쳐들었다.
266|
267|마지막 순간까지 집중해야 한다.
268|
269|“태원진가에 내놓은 자식이 있다는 풍문을 들었지. 무공은 삼류, 계집질은 일류라고. 오늘 보니 눈치도 제법이야.”
270|
271|천력부가 말했다. 도끼를 쥔 손은 느슨하게 늘어트린 채다.
272|
273|놈들의 눈에 내가 어떻게 보일지 뻔했다.
274|
275|무공은 형편없는, 가문만 좋은 한량. 텅 빈 두 손.
276|
277|천력부는 지금 방심했다.
278|
279|‘그리고 방심은 죽음이지.’
280|
281|가족들에게 월급 대부분을 보내고 고시원 단칸방에서 궁상맞게 살지만 나도 헌터다.
282|
283|F급 헌터도 게이트에서는 목숨을 걸고 싸운다. 아니, 고작 F급이라 목숨을 걸고 싸워야 한다.
284|
285|7년을 하루도 빠짐없이 싸워 온 승부사이자, 헌터라는 이름의 무림인이었다.
286|
287|그래서 안다.
288|
289|생사는 한 끗 차이라는 것을. 방심은 곧 죽음이라는 사실을.
290|
291|남은 거리가 절반으로 좁혀졌다. 서서히 발걸음이 빨라진다.
292|
293|천력부가 나를 향해 손짓한다.
294|
295|“어허. 천천히 오게, 천천히. 오다가 넘어지기라도 하면 몸값 떨어져.”
296|
297|20m.
298|
299|“두목. 쫄래쫄래 걸어오는 꼴이 꼭 강아지 같지 않습니까?”
300|

“Huh?”

*…Maybe.*

[P121]
*The other five might be even weaker than goblins.*

[P122]
At least goblins were good with poison darts. Judging by that axe throw, I had a hunch. A very strong hunch.

[P123]
I licked my parched lips, then raised both hands high.

[P124]

[P125]
“Good lad.”

[P126]
*Yeah. Laugh while you can.*

One step, two. I slowly closed the thirty-meter distance between us.

[P128]

[P129]
I could feel it just from putting one foot in front of the other.

[P130]
*It’s different!*

[P132]
The version of me inside this game was stronger than the real me.

[P133]

[P134]
I had to stay focused until the very last moment.

[P135]

The Heavenly Axe spoke with the hand holding his axe hanging loosely at his side.

[P137]
I knew exactly how I looked to them.

[P138]
A useless playboy with nothing but a good family name. Empty hands.

[P139]
The Heavenly Axe had let his guard down.

[P140]
*And letting your guard down gets you killed.*

[P141]

[P142]
Even an F-rank Hunter risked his life fighting inside Gates. No—an F-rank Hunter had to risk his life precisely because he was only F-rank.

[P143]
For seven years, I had fought every single day. I was a gambler with my life on the line—and a martial artist called a Hunter.

[P144]
So I knew.

[P145]
Life and death were separated by a hair’s breadth. Letting your guard down meant death.

[P146]
The distance had been cut in half. My steps gradually quickened.

[P147]
The Heavenly Axe beckoned me over.

[P148]
“Now, now. Take your time. If you trip on the way over, you’ll lower your ransom.”

[P149]
Twenty meters.

[P150]
“Boss, doesn’t the way he’s toddling over look just like a puppy?”

[P151]
Fifteen meters.

[P152]
“A puppy? Ha-ha-ha! You’ve got that exactly right!”

[P153]
Ten meters.

[P154]
The moment I took my next step, heat began to churn in my stomach.

[P155]
It was a sensation I had never experienced before, yet somehow, it felt strangely familiar. What was it?

[P156]
*Could it be… internal energy?*

[P157]
The heat flowing from my dantian raced toward my lower body.

[P158]
It had only one purpose: faster, lighter, stronger!

[P159]
Whoosh. I drew a long breath. My whole body tensed, every muscle drawn tight like a bowstring.

[P160]
Then came the final step.

[P161]
Boom!

[P162]
I shot straight forward. The ground cratered beneath my foot, and the sound followed after me. In that frozen moment, the Heavenly Axe’s mouth slowly fell open.

[P163]
“No way…”

[P164]
The Heavenly Axe and his underlings stared at me in disbelief.

[P165]
I could see everything about them now. Feel it.

[P166]
Their stiff, greasy hair. Their cracked lips, like a rice paddy in a drought. Their teeth—so foul-looking I could almost smell them…

[P167]
All of it.

[P168]
I found myself grinning.

[P169]
*Open Inventory. Equip Sharp Spear.*

[P170]
A cold spear shaft appeared in the hand I had thrust into empty air.

[P171]
I drove it forward with all my strength. The Heavenly Axe hastily raised his axe to block, but the sharp spearhead shattered the axe blade and punched straight through his chest.

[P172]
At the same time—

[P173]
> **System**
>

[P174]
“Ghk!”

[P175]
A fountain of blood erupted. The Heavenly Axe’s eyes trembled once, then went dark.

[P176]
> **System**

>
> Level up!
>
> You received 10 Stat Points as a level-up reward.
>
> You received 10 Skill Points as a level-up reward.
>
> Jin Family’s Cultivation Technique unlocked.

[P177]
*Whew.*

[P178]
I let out a long breath. Notifications had sounded, but all I could hear was my own pounding heart.

[P179]
One breath. Everything had happened in a single breath. I pulled the spear from the Heavenly Axe’s lifeless chest.

[P180]
*So this is possible.*

[P181]
Raise my abilities with points, enhance them with internal energy, and link them together with skills. This was the power of the System—the power that belonged to me alone.

[P182]
A power F-rank Hunter Jin Taekyung could never have dreamed of.

[P183]
*I can do this. I will.*

[P184]
The road home was beginning to look brighter and wider.

[P185]
I gripped the spear shaft and turned around.

[P186]
“So…”

[P187]
The five pairs of eyes fixed on me wavered uncertainly.

[P188]
“Anyone else want to try?”

[P189]
*The bastard who threw that axe can go first.*

[P190]
“…”

[P191]
Thud. Thud. Clatter.

[P192]
The five bandits exchanged glances, dropped their weapons, and threw themselves flat on the ground.

[P193]
“Please forgive us, Great Hero!”

[P194]

>
> The enemies have lost their will to fight and surrendered after losing their leader.
>

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). **Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.

- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.

Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. ### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.

- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. ## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

*Should I stall for time?*

[P29]
My current realm was second-rate.

[P30]
The way my body felt after distributing my stats was beyond anything I’d experienced as an F-rank Hunter, but I had no idea whether that would be enough in Murim.

[P31]
Six against one. Six against two, if I counted the coachman.

[P32]
*Could I do it?*

[P33]
There was a reason people said no one could stand against overwhelming numbers. The moment they tied up my hands and feet, I was done for.

[P34]
“How much farther is it to our destination?”

[P35]
“We’re nearly there. Another hour should be enough.”

[P36]
*Another hour…?*

[P37]
I’d suspected it, but apparently, the coachman and I had very different definitions of *nearby*.

[P38]
*What do you mean, nearly there?*

[P39]
Maybe it was because this was a continent-sized setting. The scale was different. The scale.

[P40]
Either way, I had to assume no reinforcements were coming. At least I wasn’t alone.

[P41]
The coachman’s unflappable attitude practically screamed that he was a master. Just like now.

[P42]
“Shall I handle this?”

[P43]
He coiled the horsewhip in his hand as if one crack would separate the bandits’ flesh from their bones.

[P44]
*He’s a master!*

[P45]
Of course. I was the heir of a prestigious martial family and a VIP customer of Honghwaru. There was no way they would have sent an ordinary coachman with me.

[P46]
*Wolhwa must have arranged this. She isn’t just beautiful—she’s kind, too.*

[P47]
My anxiety vanished, replaced by a pleased smile. The coachman must have taken it as permission, because the moment he turned away, a second shout rang out.

[P48]
“You bastards! Can’t you hear what the Heavenly Axe is saying?”

[P49]
I peered through the carriage window and saw a hairy man shouting with an enormous double-bladed axe in his hands. His upper body was massive, and his arms and legs were as thick as pillars.

[P50]
But the coachman muttered as if the sight were laughable.

[P51]
“Where do these little pups get off?”

[P52]
*Damn, what presence.*

[P53]
Then the coachman laid into them.

[P54]
“How dare bandits who suck the lifeblood of innocent civilians block our path! I will have you dragged before the authorities and punished to the fullest extent of the law!”

[P55]
It was a speech worthy of Judge Bao,[^1] but the hairy man—the Heavenly Axe—and his underlings didn’t seem particularly moved.

[P56]
[^1]: Judge Bao is the popular name of Bao Zheng, a Song-dynasty official celebrated in Chinese stories for his incorruptible judgments.

[P57]
“Yeah, we blocked the road. What are you going to do about it?”

[P58]
“I will gouge out your eyes, grind your limbs to powder in a mortar, and scatter the dust across the Nine Provinces! I will also exterminate all nine degrees of your kin—”

[P59]
*…Those punishments are no joke. That’s practically treason.*

[P60]
As if he had read my thoughts, the Heavenly Axe spoke up.

[P61]
“Hey, is there some member of the imperial family riding inside? Listening to you has my knees shaking. Why don’t you let us see that precious face?”

[P62]
“You will regret not retreating now once you learn this man’s identity!”

[P63]
“Okay, okay. We get it. Now come out already.”

[P64]
“You fools…!”

[P65]
The coachman clicked his tongue and turned toward me. My heart began to race. Was I finally about to see a true Murim master in action?

[P66]
“Young Master, I believe you’ll have to come out.”

[P67]
“Huh?”

[P68]
*Me? Why me?*

[P69]
“They’re the kind who won’t cry until they see the coffin. To think they would dare block your path! They’ll pay dearly for failing to recognize a master.”

[P70]
With a determined look, he opened the carriage door for me.

[P71]
“I have heard much of the Heaven Shaking Sword’s fame. A genius swordsman who reached the Peak realm at barely twenty! You cannot imagine how my old heart trembled whenever I heard stories about you, Young Master.”

[P72]
*…The Heaven Shaking Sword? A genius swordsman?*

[P73]
My thoughts tangled together. Who was the Heaven Shaking Sword? Who was this genius swordsman who had reached the Peak realm? And what the hell was this coachman playing at?

[P74]
*You said you’d handle it. Weren’t you a master?*

[P75]
“You bastards! Do you know who this man is?”

[P76]
This was bad. The coachman was barreling ahead like an eight-ton truck with a broken steering wheel.

[P77]
*No. Stop. Please stop!*

[P78]
I grabbed his wrist tightly, and he turned to look at me.

[P79]
He smiled as if he understood everything. His eyes shone with boundless trust.

[P80]
“W-wait. I’m Jin—”

[P81]
Before I could say another word, his thunderous voice rang out.

[P82]
“He is the Second Young Master of the Jin Family of Taiyuan, the Peak master whose name resounds throughout Shanxi! The Heaven Shaking Sword, Young Master Jin Mukyung!”

[P83]
“I’m Jin… Taekyung.”

[P84]
At that moment, a cold wind blew.

[P85]
“Pardon?”

[P86]
“I mean, I’m Jin Taekyung, not Jin Mukyung. And I’m the Third Young Master, not the Second…”

[P87]
“…The Third Young Master? *That* Third Young Master?”

[P88]
*Yes, you idiot.*

[P89]
The coachman’s pupils began to tremble. It was an 8.0-magnitude earthquake.

[P90]
“Th-then where is Young Master Jin Mukyung?”

[P91]
“How should I know?”

[P92]
*He’s probably sleeping at this hour.*

[P93]
The coachman stared at me with the expression of a man who had lost his country, then collapsed like a deflated inflatable toy.

[P94]
He had fainted.

[P95]
*Fuck. Some master.*

[P96]
I released his wrist.

[P97]
His wrist was as thin as a chicken bone. Something had felt off from the moment I grabbed it. He had put on quite a show, only to turn out to be an ordinary civilian.

[P98]
“Ha! Ha-ha-ha!”

[P99]
The bandits roared with laughter. My back was already damp with cold sweat, and I hadn’t even noticed when it started.

[P100]
*If I’m really unlucky here…*

[P101]
I couldn’t bring myself to say the word *death*. I swallowed hard.

[P102]
I swept my tense gaze over the bandits.

[P103]
*Fuck. I’d rather fight six goblins than deal with this. How am I supposed to beat guys that huge…?*

[P104]
Wait.

[P105]
“Huh?”

[P106]
Was it my imagination? No. No matter how I looked at them, it wasn’t.

[P107]
Massive upper bodies. Thick arms and legs. And… short.

[P108]
The other five weren’t much different. The Heavenly Axe at least had a decent physique, but the rest were about five hundred light-years away from anything you could call “well-built.”

[P109]
In other words, the bandits were built exactly like…

[P110]
“They’re goblins?”

[P111]
*Goblins?*

[P112]
I stood there dazed for a moment until an axe came flying at me and snapped me back to reality. They had the numbers, and they were launching a preemptive attack too?

[P113]
“Hey, hey! Time out!”

[P114]
The axe struck the ground a good ten meters short of me. No—it didn’t even stick. It toppled over. The bandit who had thrown it scratched the back of his head sheepishly.

[P115]
“Should I have aimed a little higher?”

[P116]
*…Maybe.*

[P117]
*I might actually survive this.*

[P118]
The monster I had fought more than any other over the past seven years was the goblin.

[P119]
Naturally, I knew them inside and out. They were even the reason I had chosen a spear as my primary weapon when I was a novice Hunter. Its reach gave me an overwhelming advantage.

[P120]
And these bandits were exactly that size. To me, they no longer looked like bandits. They looked like six goblins. The Heavenly Axe was about the size of a goblin chieftain.

[P121]
*The other five might be even weaker than goblins.*

[P122]
At least goblins were good with poison darts. Judging by that axe throw, I had a hunch. A very strong hunch.

[P123]
I licked my parched lips, then raised both hands high.

[P124]
A few of them looked confused by my gesture of surrender, while the Heavenly Axe smiled proudly, like a father welcoming his son home from military service.

[P125]
“Good lad.”

[P126]
*Yeah. Laugh while you can.*

[P127]
One step, two. I slowly closed the thirty-meter distance between us.

[P128]
With a steady stride and balanced posture. One breath per step. My breath streamed out into the dawn air.

[P129]
I could feel it just from putting one foot in front of the other.

[P130]
*It’s different!*

[P131]
I realized it once more.

[P132]
The version of me inside this game was stronger than the real me.

[P133]
My heart pounded. At the same time, caution stirred in the back of my mind.

[P134]
I had to stay focused until the very last moment.

[P135]
“I heard the Jin Family had a son they’d given up on. Third-rate at martial arts, first-rate with women. Now that I see you, you’ve got pretty good instincts too.”

[P136]
The Heavenly Axe spoke with the hand holding his axe hanging loosely at his side.

[P137]
I knew exactly how I looked to them.

[P138]
A useless playboy with nothing but a good family name. Empty hands.

[P139]
The Heavenly Axe had let his guard down.

[P140]
*And letting your guard down gets you killed.*

[P141]
I might send most of my salary to my family and live miserably in a tiny goshiwon room, but I was still a Hunter.

[P142]
Even an F-rank Hunter risked his life fighting inside Gates. No—an F-rank Hunter had to risk his life precisely because he was only F-rank.

[P143]
For seven years, I had fought every single day. I was a gambler with my life on the line—and a martial artist called a Hunter.

[P144]
So I knew.

[P145]
Life and death were separated by a hair’s breadth. Letting your guard down meant death.

[P146]
The distance had been cut in half. My steps gradually quickened.

[P147]
The Heavenly Axe beckoned me over.

[P148]
“Now, now. Take your time. If you trip on the way over, you’ll lower your ransom.”

[P149]
Twenty meters.

[P150]
“Boss, doesn’t the way he’s toddling over look just like a puppy?”

[P151]
Fifteen meters.

[P152]
“A puppy? Ha-ha-ha! You’ve got that exactly right!”

[P153]
Ten meters.

[P154]
The moment I took my next step, heat began to churn in my stomach.

[P155]
It was a sensation I had never experienced before, yet somehow, it felt strangely familiar. What was it?

[P156]
*Could it be… internal energy?*

[P157]
The heat flowing from my dantian raced toward my lower body.

[P158]
It had only one purpose: faster, lighter, stronger!

[P159]
Whoosh. I drew a long breath. My whole body tensed, every muscle drawn tight like a bowstring.

[P160]
Then came the final step.

[P161]
Boom!

[P162]
I shot straight forward. The ground cratered beneath my foot, and the sound followed after me. In that frozen moment, the Heavenly Axe’s mouth slowly fell open.

[P163]
“No way…”

[P164]
The Heavenly Axe and his underlings stared at me in disbelief.

[P165]
I could see everything about them now. Feel it.

[P166]
Their stiff, greasy hair. Their cracked lips, like a rice paddy in a drought. Their teeth—so foul-looking I could almost smell them…

[P167]
All of it.

[P168]
I found myself grinning.

[P169]
*Open Inventory. Equip Sharp Spear.*

[P170]
A cold spear shaft appeared in the hand I had thrust into empty air.

[P171]
I drove it forward with all my strength. The Heavenly Axe hastily raised his axe to block, but the sharp spearhead shattered the axe blade and punched straight through his chest.

[P172]
At the same time—

[P173]
> **System**
>
> Critical hit! Status effect Bleeding activated!

[P174]
“Ghk!”

[P175]
A fountain of blood erupted. The Heavenly Axe’s eyes trembled once, then went dark.

[P176]
> **System**
>
> Lv. 10 Jang Sam defeated.
>
> Level up!
>
> You received 10 Stat Points as a level-up reward.
>
> You received 10 Skill Points as a level-up reward.
>
> Jin Family’s Cultivation Technique unlocked.

[P177]
*Whew.*

[P178]
I let out a long breath. Notifications had sounded, but all I could hear was my own pounding heart.

[P179]
One breath. Everything had happened in a single breath. I pulled the spear from the Heavenly Axe’s lifeless chest.

[P180]
*So this is possible.*

[P181]
Raise my abilities with points, enhance them with internal energy, and link them together with skills. This was the power of the System—the power that belonged to me alone.

[P182]
A power F-rank Hunter Jin Taekyung could never have dreamed of.

[P183]
*I can do this. I will.*

[P184]
The road home was beginning to look brighter and wider.

[P185]
I gripped the spear shaft and turned around.

[P186]
“So…”

[P187]
The five pairs of eyes fixed on me wavered uncertainly.

[P188]
“Anyone else want to try?”

[P189]
*The bastard who threw that axe can go first.*

[P190]
“…”

[P191]
Thud. Thud. Clatter.

[P192]
The five bandits exchanged glances, dropped their weapons, and threw themselves flat on the ground.

[P193]
“Please forgive us, Great Hero!”

[P194]
> **System**
>
> The enemies have lost their will to fight and surrendered after losing their leader.
>
> Defeat the Bandits complete.
>
> You have fully recovered from all fatigue and injuries.
>
> You have defeated the bandits. Fame increased by 10.
>
> Tutorial—Stage 3 complete. Rewards will be distributed.
>
> Chain Quest Tutorial—Stage 4 created.

[P195]
*Now I can finally catch my breath.*

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.

- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.

- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.

- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.
